_why: Operator STANDING ORDER 2026-11-03 (verbatim): 'Failed CI now gets ONE automatic re-run by agents, no asking: gh run rerun <id> --failed. Pass on re-run = FLAKY, record the test name and run ids, OPEN A FIX TASK so it becomes deterministic, and carry on. Fail again = REAL, never re-run a third time, fix it first. One re-run per failing head per check so red is never retried into green.' This SUPERSEDES the earlier §28.14 'never a test failure' reading: rerun_classes.test_failure is now true, bounded to one rerun per (head, check group) by the lane's rerun ledger, and a passing re-run opens a LOCAL fixer request (the fix task) so the test becomes deterministic. The GitHub flaky-test issue stays off (a remote write from a scheduled job, §24.5); the fix task is the durable fixer_requests/<run id>.json the self-heal fixer consumes. A rerun that fails again is REAL: never re-run a third time.
_required_workflows_why: Workflow DISPLAY names from .github/workflows/*.yml, not check-run names. The required check contexts are cio-hardening (job in cio-production-hardening-ci, also reported by cio-full-suite-sharded), agent-governance, release-readiness and ci-gate (the aggregate job in cio-full-suite-sharded); gh run list reports workflow names, so both files are listed. config/release_train_delegation.example.json carries the check-context list.
_rerun_classes_why: infrastructure = the run died for a reason a rerun can plausibly clear (startup_failure, timed_out, or a log marker below). test_failure = one automatic re-run per failing HEAD per check group (operator standing order 2026-11-03, quoted in _why): a passing re-run is FLAKY and opens a local fix task; a second failure is REAL and is never re-run a third time. unknown stays false: an unclassified failure could be anything and has no deterministic retry story.
infra_log_markers: The runner has received a shutdown signal

flaky_issue.label: flaky-test
flaky_issue._why: Opening or commenting on a GitHub issue is a remote write from a scheduled job (§24.5). Off until the operator ratifies an amendment; the suspected flake is still recorded in the receipt and the local runs.jsonl.

fixer._why: A durable request file, never a push or a PR from this lane (AGENTS.md 24.5, 28.14). fixer_requests/<run id>.json is an incident document in the exact shape scripts/self_heal_fixer.py --cycle --incident already consumes (N8nCodeDefect@v1 + a RunReceipt@v2-shaped receipt + registry_row); a test runs that fixer in dry-run over the request and asserts it admits one fix_requested job. The fixer still stops at a local fix branch until the operator arms it; when armed, its fix PR follows the merge gate (scripts/lib/pr_all_checks_green.py).

_page_groups_why: The two workflows run the same hardening suite; a page is deduplicated by (head SHA, group) so one red commit pages once, not once per workflow.
